changes.to:
Per docs/adr/0001-satellites-never-extend-core-formats.md, templates must NOT carry editor-specific fields (no dragPos values, no named v-drag anchors, no parallel .md template format).

The TemplateEditor instead:
- Derives draggable handles from existing template structure: {{slot}} placeholders and sldr-* classed elements are the anchors (the DOM is already enumerable).
- Writes positions back as standard CSS (grid areas, order, alignment) — the core's existing layout language. The editor manipulates what the format already expresses: slot arrangement, alignment, grid. No free pixel coordinates / absolute positioning.
- Keeps editor-only state (snap grids, selection, UI hints) in Octo's own files, never in core templates.

Templates remain the core .html format in crates/sldr-renderer/templates/. Any new template shipped for Octo demos (title-slide, code-demo, comparison, ...) is a plain core template that must make sense to a user who has never seen Octo.

changes.from:
Asymmetry vs layouts. Layouts ship as embedded BUILTIN_LAYOUTS resolved at runtime (override by user file). Flavors have NO built-in tier (only `default`): load_flavor searches disk only, so the 21 bundled flavors must be bulk-written to ~/.config/sldr/flavors on `init` to be usable.

Consequence (now visible via `sldr show`): those copies are frozen at the sldr version that ran init. `sldr show flavor aurora` resolves to the stale config copy, not the binary — a later improved built-in never reaches the user, with no built-in tier beneath to fall back to. Silent staleness.

Proposal: add embedded flavors as a real lowest-priority resolution tier in load_flavor (mirror LayoutRegistry::builtin). Then `init` need not bulk-write them; user materializes one on demand via `sldr flavor fork/eject` (trx-r72j) which overrides by name. Single source of truth, no drift, flavors↔layouts symmetric. Open question the user is weighing: keep on-disk install for raw-file legibility (cat/grep the whole catalog) vs binary-only + `show`. `show` now covers per-item legibility either way.
changes.to: DECIDED (won't change): keep the bundled flavors installed to disk and editable. They are seeds, not sacred — edit/rename/delete freely; `sldr init --force` re-installs/overwrites the bundled set to restore or refresh them. No runtime built-in tier needed; the on-disk install IS the model. Per-item legibility is covered by `sldr show flavor <name>` (trx-9wqc). Layouts stay built-in + overridable; `sldr show layout <name>` reads them and piping to a file forks one.

changes.from:
The deck renders fill-the-window responsive (.sldr-deck = 100vw x 100vh; type in vw/vh/clamp; onResize is a no-op). So a slide looks different at every viewport width AND aspect ratio — the browser window (often taller than 16:9) vs the fixed 16:9 PDF page. Symptoms: PDF font sizes differ from the browser and content overflows on some slides.

Mitigation shipped (0.6.x): export renders at @page 1920x1080 so vw/vh land near a maximized-laptop browser (less overflow, closer type). Not a true fix.

Proper fix: a fixed 16:9 design canvas, letterboxed and scaled to fit on screen, so what you author IS what exports. Blocker: ~380 vw/vh occurrences (101 base.css + 78 layouts + 203 user/example flavors) are viewport-relative. Options: (a) container-query units (cqw/cqh) with the slide as container — cleanest but requires converting every vw/vh incl. user flavors; (b) render the deck in a fixed-size (1920x1080) iframe scaled to fit — vw/vh resolve against the iframe so NO unit conversion needed, but a bigger presenter-architecture change (nav/keyboard across the frame). Decide (a) vs (b).
changes.to: REJECTED in favor of adaptive fit-to-body. Tommy wants to keep responsive/adaptive sizing, NOT a fixed canvas. Instead: (1) delimit each layout's content "body" region; (2) auto-fit (shrink-to-fit) the content to that region so it never overflows at any viewport; (3) chrome zones (headline/subheadline) get reserved space so they never collide with logos. New issue tracks this. Fixed-canvas / iframe approach abandoned.

changes.to:
sldr studio: the interactive authoring satellite. Design: docs/adr/0009-sldr-studio-api-first-web-satellite.md.
Refreshes the original (slidev-era) Octo integration onto sldr's native renderer.

Shape:
- Satellite (ADR-0001): writes only canonical files; mechanical, not curation; disposable.
- API-first: sldr-server (axum) is the contract — slides/playlists/flavors/build/preview + layouts CRUD + zone parse/emit. CLI + decks stay pure-Rust / node-free.
- Frontend = the existing Oqto `sldr` app (apps/sldr) built out, reusing Oqto's design system (vendor/design-system, synced by `byt`), authFetch Bearer token, React Query, Tailwind 4. Reached from a phone via Oqto over Tailscale.
- Auth: light bearer token, Tailscale-only (not public-hardened).

Three sections:
1. Slide management + deck building (mobile-first)
2. Flavor editor on the current token model (type_scale, density, per-role sizes, chrome_layouts, .sldr-chrome) — REPLACES the scrapped `sldr flavor`
3. Layout editor — HTML + scoped CSS + a visual PPTX-zone editor emitting `<!-- sldr:zone -->`

Carried forward (done): sldr-server crate, Octo route mounting, SlideLibrary component.
